#3951. Steam's new Steam Deck framerate graphs are good news for handheld players, though I wouldn't fully trust the numbers yet

Valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck. Or, rather, a framerate average-r, as games on the Steam Store are now getting attached graphs – under their existing Steam Deck Compatibility details – that show how many frames-per-secondseses that game has been recording on real players' handhelds, the OLED and original LCD models both.

The thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide. This may induce some gentle learned nodding, if you've ever tried an Unsupported game only to find it works more or less fine, or have ever wondered why a game that can just about scrape 30fps together gets the same green good-job sticker as something that screams along at 90fps. Now, when checking that rating, you'll also get a relatively specific idea of smoothness and/or chugging potential.

Or will you? By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates. The scoundrel. My current handheld game beau, Mortal Shell II, looks like it may be falling victim to this: its results for the LCD Steam Deck show it mostly runs around 30fps, which is in line with my experience, but the OLED results show it averaging around 45fps. The Steam Deck OLED's APU is a tiny bit quicker than the LCD Deck's, but it's not that much of an upgrade.

There's work to be done, then, though I do appreciate the concept. As tightly as I cling to my battery-efficient, mercifully Windows-free Deck OLED in the face of drastically more powerful handhelds, with every year it becomes a little less likely that new games will comfortably run on it. Verification ratings can still act as decent (if broad) guidelines, but even with V-Sync putting an immaculately untorn thumb on the scales, game-specific framerate data will be much more illustrative.

As for whether these histograms will also get Steam Machine versions, or perhaps cover non-Valve handhelds, Valve say this: "We see this update as a stepping stone toward providing framerate data for more devices than just Steam Deck. To this end, we are also prompting customers to opt-in to providing anonymized framerate data in the Steam desktop client. This opt-in is currently only on Steam Client Beta, and will ship to all customers in the future." So, maybe, if you gizzus yer data.

#3950. Guide: GTA 6 Release Times: When Can You Start Playing?

Probably the most anticipated game of all time, GTA 6 is now just hours away! We're in the final home stretch now, with availability rolling out on PS5 worldwide within the next 24 hours.

As the launch draws even closer, we're covering absolutely everything you need to know about its PS5 launch, including preload options and release times. In this GTA 6 guide, we cover the GTA 6 release times.

On this page: GTA 6 Release Times: When Can You Start Playing?

Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 will officially be playable from midnight on 19th November in your local time zone. If you have preloaded the game, it'll unlock at midnight, and then you can begin playing immediately.

Review GTA 6 (PS5) - The Greatest Open World Game Ever Made

As such, the game will unlock and be available first in New Zealand. Availability will then roll out worldwide as each time zone reaches midnight on 19th November.

When the game launches in the UK, we'll have a hub live on the home page documenting our coverage and providing a place for you to share your first experiences with GTA 6.

GTA 6 preload is available now! If you've pre-ordered from the PS Store, your download of the game should have started and will then be ready for you to start playing at release.

Rockstar has now officially confirmed the GTA 6 file size on PS5, and what you'll need to download, is 212GB. This is one of the biggest downloads and installs on console in history, and will probably only get bigger through patches and the addition of GTA Online.

GTA 6 will unlock and be playable in New Zealand first, as it's located in one of the furthest along timezones. The chances are New Zealand is further along in the day compared to wherever you live in the world, so yes, New Zealand will be the first to gain access to GTA 6.

Because of this, there's been a rising trend in people creating New Zealand PSN account to play games as soon as possible. This can be done with GTA 6 too, but you'll need to set up a fresh New Zealand PSN account and buy the game through its PS Store.

When you have done, you'll be able to play GTA 6 a few hours ahead of other countries like the USA. Keep in mind, though, that you can't transfer your save data from the New Zealand account you set up to your normal profile.

If you were to play GTA 6 early via the New Zealand method detailed above, you get access to the game at these times:North America: 3am PST / 4am MST / 5am CST / 6am ESTUK/Ire: 11am GMTEurope: 12pm CET / 1pm EETAsia/Oceania: 8pm JST / 7pm AWST / 10pm AEDT

GTA 6 is available digitally on the PS Store, or in a basic physical version that ships without a disc. The latter provides a code in the box that you redeem on the PS Store to get the digital version.

The two PS5 digital versions on offer are: Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition.

Ultimate Edition / Ultimate Edition Upgrade Contents:

Rockstar is only selling GTA 6 in a digital format; you can't buy the game on a physical disc in any way. Even the version you buy in retail shops or from online retailers won't contain a disc. Instead, the actual GTA 6 box will have a code inside you can use to download the game. There's no version with a physical disc of any kind.

Rockstar has now confirmed a GTA 6 map will be made available, but it won't be included in the physical versions like for previous games. Instead, a physical GTA 6 map will be put on the official Rockstar store for $0.99. Or, it'll be included for free in all other purchases from the storefront.

Have you pre-ordered GTA 6, and will you be staying up to play at midnight? Let us know in the comments below.

#3949. Review: GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

This is going to dominate your life for months!

Where do you even start with a game like GTA 6? Not only is it the most highly-anticipated video game we've ever seen, but it's also attempting to live up to ridiculous expectations set by its predecessors over the years. GTA 3 revolutionised how we thought about 3D open-world epics, Vice City and San Andreas pushed things to the next level, GTA 4 took yet another massive step into the HD era, and GTA 5 propelled the series into another stratosphere.

We've all spent the last 13 years trying to figure out what GTA 6 might look like by the time it arrives, and the answer is perhaps more simplistic than some had theorised - it's basically GTA 5 mixed with Red Dead Redemption 2, but with a ton of added detail and ambition on top. That's all it needed to be, and I reckon people are going to absolutely love it.

Before we get to the open world, which is surely the most incredible aspect of the entire game, we should first touch on the story of Lucia and Jason. These two amateur criminals accidentally run into each other and establish a relationship (which can alter between platonic and romantic depending on how you interact throughout the campaign), and after a simple score goes wrong, they find themselves being dragged into more and more dangerous scenarios. That's the basic premise, and the rest is up for you to discover yourself.

The GTA 6 Extended Preview from a few months ago left me very concerned about whether there was enough intrigue to the two main characters (along with the NPCs for that matter), but I needn't have worried. Lucia is a fiesty, hot-headed personality - the type of person who thinks less about the consequences and more about the high life she's determined to acquire - while Jason is extremely laid back to a hilarious extent at times, although also highly capable in pretty much any situation he finds himself in. The two bounce off each other really nicely, and their dynamic definitely remains engaging throughout the campaign's duration.

While I really don't want to spoil anything story-related, the mission structure is very much what you'd expect from GTA 5 and RDR2. In other words, there's a well-balanced mix of laid-back and humorous missions along with more intense shootouts and getaways that significantly ramp up in intensity. They've managed to get really inventive and ambitious with some of the later missions in particular, and I think there's no doubt they're the best of any GTA game.

I also want to point out the use of music in GTA 6's missions, which caught me off-guard and became one of my low-key favourite features. In a nutshell, if you find yourself in the likes of a shootout or a getaway, you'll often notice that curated tunes play in the background to amplify the situation. The developers sometimes even go a step further by making the lighting around you pulsate to the beat, or by introducing lyricists to create a menacing vibe, and it can turn an otherwise generic mission into an amazing one. Seriously, I can't overstate how much I love this feature.

The story itself takes 40ish hours if you completely rush it (which admittedly I've been doing for the most part to hit this embargo), but if you take your time and do at least a decent amount of the optional stuff, it's likely more around 60-100+ hours. As I say, I've enjoyed all of those hours, and I think the campaign seriously hits its stride in the final third - the vast majority of memorable moments are saved for the latter stages.

I don't want you to fixate on the 40-100+ hour figure though, and that's because GTA 6's open world is so incredible and so vast that you could be playing it for months, and likely years, and not see everything it has to offer. We've never seen a GTA world like this - traffic levels are extremely high, the number of NPCs on the streets is ridiculous, it always feels like something's happening around every corner (there are so many random encounters!), you'll find loads of buildings you can go into, there's so much detail on everything... it's just an absolute dream for anyone who loves the idea of immersing themselves in this game.

GTA 5 had an amazing open world too, but after going back and playing it for the purpose of this review, there are two major differences that stand out - there's far less actually happening in the world at any one time (and therefore much less to interact with), and the map just feels tiny in comparison. GTA 6's state of Leonida incorporates so much more than just Vice City itself, including many other highly-populated areas such as Key Lento and Ambrosia. The first time you actually see Vice City in a mission (assuming you haven't gone and explored it previously) is a highlight of the entire game - it immediately appears so vast and so incredibly detailed that it feels like a next-gen experience.

The way in which you interact with that world as a player has evolved as well. Cops are smarter than ever, and not only prove a tough challenge when attempting a getaway at three stars or more, but they also remember what you look like - and therefore you sometimes have to disguise yourself by changing into different outfits. Stealing a car now requires you to think about what kind of lock system it has on it, and whether there's a tracker fitted that will alert the police to your location. Cars can even run out of fuel now! Every element feels more in-depth than we've seen in GTA in the past, but Rockstar has crucially balanced the impact just right, so it's never to the detriment of your ability to just have fun.

I do think you'll get the most out of the game if you pace yourself though. It feels intentionally designed to encourage a slow playstyle where you explore, hang out, browse the fully-featured social media and news feeds on your phone (complete with video clips and comment sections), take part in games like pool and minigolf, engage in countless side-missions and random encounters, watch and play a ridiculous amount of purpose-built content on your in-game TV, and ultimately just see what you can discover without rapidly jumping from mission-to-mission. The amount of content here is overwhelming, but in a really satisfying way.

Of course, it's almost a given at this point that GTA 6 looks visually incredible, and I can confirm that it's definitely a stunner on Xbox Series X. There's some occasional pop-in, but it's minimal, and I only ran into a few tiny bugs during the review period (which may have been ironed out for release anyway). The performance is mostly very smooth considering the circumstances as well - yes, it's a bit jarring at first to go back to 30FPS if you've been playing 60FPS games for the most part in recent years, but give it an hour-or-two, and you probably won't care anymore. Seriously, it's a total non-issue for me at this point, and I'm more than happy playing at 30FPS.

It should be noted that I played around 30 hours on a VRR-enabled display during the review period, and around 10 hours without one. I was perfectly happy with the performance in both cases, with the only noticeably big frame rate drops occurring during very rare and visually intensive gameplay sequences.

So, is there anything I don't like about GTA 6? The only thing I'd say is that it doesn't top my tier list in terms of greatest GTA stories ever, although it's probably still in the top three. It's a narrative that'll fully invest most players from start to finish, and there are shocking moments and twists that are bound to last long in the memory, but I also reckon it gets a bit too convoluted and farcical at times. That said, the final third of the campaign is jam-packed with intense story elements and incredibly action-packed missions, guaranteeing some truly jaw-dropping moments.

Its tone can also feel overly harsh and uncomfortably serious in specific circumstances, but hey... this is Grand Theft Auto after all. Every GTA has its moments like that, but the impact feels more striking this time due to the enhanced sense of realism. Fortunately, there's plenty of lighthearted humour to be found along the way as well.

Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come. It's coupled with a campaign that's full of extremely entertaining missions, led by two main characters who I've become much more invested in than I'd anticipated.

I'd have been fuming if you'd told me in 2013 that I'd have to wait 13 more years for the next GTA game, but now that it's finally here, I'm just relieved they've somehow managed to pull off another Game of the Decade contender once again.

#3948. Tripwire Interactive says it's laying off 36 staff in a "necessary" decision, while reassuring that Killing Floor 3 and Maneater 2 are still in active development

In a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have announced that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find new jobs quickly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

Despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

This news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.

#3947. "A fight for all workers": SAG-AFTRA throw weight behind emerging Rockstar union ahead of its GTA 6 release week vote

In what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies."

If it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting important leverage from a global force.

SAG-AFTRA's statement declares that "unionisation is vital for the future of the video game industry", and that "in the face of record layoffs, job instability, hostile work places, and toxic crunch culture, it is now more critical than ever for unions and workers to stand in support of one another." They advocate for fair treatment, especially in the wake of displacement due to corporate mismanagement and genAI, and proudly state that "this is a fight for all workers."

Their statement closes by saying that "the gaming industry is a commercial juggernaut, and the people that create these amazing works of art deserve fair treatment and the opportunity to improve the terms of their employment with a strong voice at the bargaining table. We honor the courage of our fellow game workers at Rockstar and proudly support their union vote."

Solidarity with the workers, always. We can only wait and see how the voting process pans out.

"I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he'd be "honored" to return as CEO of the company in a new statement addressing the "mistakes" that led to this whole mess – notably, multiple reported affairs.

"Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met," Huang says in a tweet. "Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me."

Huang admits, "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation."

Pertinently, he responds to widespread calls – many made by Nvidia employees – to have him "return as CEO."

"Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics," Huang says. "NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."

As CNN reports, US President Donald Trump previously said he "would not mind" if Huang was reinstated as CEO. However, CNBC reports the Nvidia board is not interested in Huang's return.

#3944. In a reveal that might worry eventual PC players glancing at their GPUs, GTA 6 will target 30fps on all consoles

Oh, and and it'll be streamable on the Xbox One before it's playable on PC

In a press release coinciding with Grand Theft Auto VI becoming available for pre-load ahead of its November 19th release date, Rockstar has confirmed that the game "has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits." Read between the lines, and you can kind of make out the words "...so hope your PCs are up to spec, computer nerds."

GTA 6, of course, still does not have a confirmed PC version, even if Rockstar's former tech director says it's probably not far off. And despite this, even ancient, last-gen consoles are getting in on it, as the release also unexpectedly confirms that the game will be playable on Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming, Microsoft's game streaming service that has suddenly lost its ability to work on PC. Granted, this comes with a warning: "as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay." If you ended up getting a PS4 last generation, no cloud play for you either, I'm afraid. It also states that it will "play best on Playstation 5 consoles", making great use of that Sony partnership, and will include Playstation Spectral Super Resolution and ray-traced shadows on PS5 Pro.

A 2026 current-gen game targeting 30fps, let alone one as titanic of a release as GTA VI, is probably not going to go down well with a lot of people, even if console players are traditionally les sensitive about FPS counts than PC players. What this does imply, though, is that the inevitable PC release might be an even more demanding behemoth than expected, if Xbox Series and PS5 versions can't even target 60fps. The availability of the game on Xbox One, even if just through cloud streaming, could have resulted in an acceptance that 60fps just wasn't going to be possible if it was also going to be able to 'run' on last-gen hardware. Either way, when it does eventually escape console exclusivity, hopefully trying to run GTA VI on anything less than an RTX 5080 won't set your PC on fire. Now, let me just quickly have a glance at GPU prices. Oh, no.

#3943. Roundup: Here's What The Critics Are Saying About GTA 6 So Far

Are we looking at the highest-rated game of 2026?

The first reviews for GTA 6 are officially out now, and as you've probably already seen, we've got one here at Pure Xbox! We gave the game an "Outstanding" 10/10, which isn't entirely surprising considering the history of this series.

But what about everyone else? GTA 6 is nominated for Game of the Year at The Game Awards, so does it live up to that recommendation? Are the critics overwhelmingly enamoured with it? That's what we've been intrigued to find out.

So, here's what the critics are saying about GTA 6 so far:

"Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come."

Review GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

This is going to dominate your life for months!

"GTA 6 is the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar has set a new sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time."

Review GTA 6 (PS5) - The Greatest Open World Game Ever Made

"A game so good I asked our tech team if I could somehow give it 11/10. GTA 6 is an absolute masterclass in genre-mashing. With meticulous detailing and levels of immersion that almost feel dangerous, it's steeped in steamy satire — with story beats that often cut close to home as they relish in laugh-out-loud absurdity. Given the state of the industry, it's sobering that we might never see another game like this again. Grand Theft Auto 6 is a cover-to-cover masterpiece without equal."

"Grand Theft Auto VI is a generational game that stands toe-to-toe with many of the great crime stories and satires across other media. It showcases both the entertainment value of interactive play and the current high-water mark for technical and artistic detail in games. Hunt for and count up all the minor faults or foibles you like, but then note how you just spent another hour lost in this remarkable escape into criminality, wanton violence, egregious sex, and the elusive potential of true love."

"This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7."

"GTA 6 is the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation. Rockstar has built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality. There's a degree of sophistication to everything GTA 6 does, and there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments."

"I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that."

"Grand Theft Auto VI delivers a remarkably immersive and ambitious open-world experience, blending thrilling gameplay, diverse activities, and a compelling relationship between Jason and Lucia. While uneven storytelling, pacing issues, and occasional performance drops prevent it from reaching perfection, the richly realized world of Leonida and its extraordinary attention to detail make this an unforgettable crime adventure that largely lives up to its monumental expectations."

"Grand Theft Auto VI is a great game that lives up to so much of the hype and expectations. Lucia and Jason are a well-written and compelling pair of protagonists, and the side characters you meet on their journey are great, even if the need to constantly raise the stakes across such a long story lessens its impact. You do have so much more freedom with how to tackle missions, though, and Leonida is a world filled with things to do and discover that will keep you coming back for a long time."

As you can see, GTA 6 is a darling of the critics right now, and its initial rating on Metacritic sits at a whopping 99, which makes it the highest-rated game of 2026 (and literally the joint best game of all time if it keeps up this pace).

It should be noted that the vast majority of reviews are for the PS5 version, but both the PlayStation and Xbox versions are both sitting at 99 as things stand. That figure will probably change, but not to any significant degree.

History tells us that we should have always expected a mainline Grand Theft Auto game to get incredible review scores, but it was really hard to see how they'd live up to expectations with this one. Nevertheless, they've somehow done it!

#3942. GTA 6 Requires New PS5 Firmware Update to Play

As we reported early yesterday, PS5 has a new firmware update, numbered v14.23.00. It’s now confirmed you’ll need to have this installed to play GTA 6.

Notifying players on social media, a PlayStation Support page said: “Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing GTA 6. Players should download this update prior to midnight on 19th November so that they’re ready to play on launch day, 19th November.”

Sony usually gives users a period of grace to play their games before a new firmware update is made mandatory, so this is unprecedented behaviour.

But the stakes have never been higher either: Rockstar’s open world is the most anticipated game of all time, and it’s coming at a time when the PS5 has been cracked wide open.

Sony’s currently in a cat-and-mouse battle with hackers, as it tries to shore up the security of its console.

That all comes at the cost of inconvenience to the rest of us, as we’re forced to install firmware updates which have been coming more and more frequently of late.

This latest version is just 1.3GB so it’s not a huge lift, but this is your 24 hour warning that you’ll need to have it installed to play GTA 6.

#3941. Bandai Namco is liquidating Unknown 9: Awakening studio Reflector Entertainment, following multiple previous layoffs since the game's launch

As another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco announced in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening. In its notice, Bandai Namco explains that the reason for the liquidation is due to Reflector not meeting its expectations for "future business plans, necessary additional investment, and the possibility of profitability and business continuation."

The press release notes that the liquidation of Reflector will result in an estimated "extraordinary loss" of around 21 million euros, or 3.5 billion yen, for Bandai Namco in its Q3 fiscal report of this year. This is not the first time Reflector has been cut by Bandai, as around a month after the launch of Unknown 9: Awakening and presumably in response to its low sales, 18% of the workforce was laid off. 2025 then saw further redundancies amidst the cancellation of a prospective project, though details on those layoffs were not granted by the company. Unknown 9 was intended to be a transmedia franchise involving the game as well as comic books and novels, but these ambitions never came to pass.

Bandai Namco notes that the liquidation will be held to local laws and procedures, which make the actual schedule of the process uncertain for now. A similar process faces Arkane Lyon, which is currently in a purgatory of having been chosen for closure by Microsoft, but temporarily protected by French labor laws that prevent it from being suddenly closed without proper negotiation and procedure.

#3940. Company of Heroes 3 developer admits "it was a lot" to make the 3.0 overhaul patch alongside regular updates, singleplayer DLC, and a whole spinoff game

The Company of Heroes 3's 3.0 update is huge. Touching virtually every part of the three-year-old RTS, the patch notes are longer than, well, my arm isn't a great measure of patch note length. Let's just say the headline features of overhauled VFX and audio don't really cover it. It also comes with new autumn and winter biomes, an updated grand strategy campaign, improvements to unit AI, and a whole host of other changes.

Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.

The team began planning the 3.0 update two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Company of Heroes 3, and focus on issues players had flagged since launch. "The VFX were called out," executive producer Denise Christie tells me. "Same thing with a lot of our audio."

Relic were already releasing patches every three months, but the changes they were looking at were much too large for those smaller updates. If they had tried to do the work as part of the small updates, approaching the problems with piecemeal solutions, it would have turned Company of Heroes 3 into a hodgepodge of new and old assets. "We wanted to make sure it was a cohesive package," principal designer Eric Wrobel says. "If you increase the quality of one thing, you have to do it equally across so much stuff." Otherwise you end up with "One that looks awesome and one that's like, 'Oh, this one's kind of gross'."

Complicating matters, though, was that the team couldn't down tools and focus on just these large changes. As well as the small patches that were still going out every three months, both the VFX and audio teams were also contributing the battlegroup DLC packs which added new units to the game. "They would work on stuff and in one branch that was the 3.0 work and then they would go ahead and do some battlegroup stuff and come back to that," Christie says. "It was a lot."

As the 3.0 update grew in scope, it also meant other departments were contributing to the anniversary release while working on the smaller updates and DLC. "For us to create future maps for Company of Heroes 3, we were going to have an issue that our assets were getting stale," Christie explains. So, as part of 3.0, Relic's art department created autumn and winter asset packs, as well as a new Industrial theme. This then created more work for the VFX team, who have added rain and snow, as well as a transition effect showing soil and concrete moving from dry to wet.

Not to be outdone, the design team also made significant changes to the singleplayer Italy campaign. The towns that dot the dynamic grand strategy-inspired map now have individual upgrades, making for more meaningful decisions when it comes to which settlement you capture next. And, responding to one of the main criticisms of Company of Heroes 3's singleplayer, they also updated the computer's AI so it makes smarter decisions in both the turn-based and real-time battles. "We wanted to get this feel like there was that sort of back and forth of the AI resisting you and pushing forward into your territory and actually taking your stuff, which wasn't really happening in any of the previous updates," Wrobel says.

Further complicating matters was the fact that alongside these regular updates, the DLC, and the big 3.0 update release work, was that Relic also released Final Stand in July, a roguelike horde mode spinoff of Company of Heroes 3. "We had to be very careful not to accidentally introduce this 3.0 work that was also happening at the same time," Christie says." The improvements in this update have also rolled out for the spinoff, too.

Naturally, Relic aren't doing all this work purely out of the goodness of the hearts. The regular updates keep players engaged, Christie explains, and "hopefully bring back lapsed players who were frustrated by some of these things." It's something the team have already seen happen before, Wrobel explains. "We saw with the 2.0 update that we had a big spike of users and that was great, but because that improved the overall quality of the game, we saw each month we were selling more copies than we were before. People have been buying these games for years and years and years, so if we invest in this now we're going to see returns for quite a long time into the future as well."

"If we were starting to see that tail down then we probably would have made a very different decision to be honest, but that's not what we see," Christie adds.

The next release for Company of Heroes 3 is a singleplayer DLC, Operation Torch, due out on November 25th. (So, if you're keeping count, that was also in the works while the update, battlegroup DLC, and spinoff were all being made.) Until now, Relic's additions to the RTS have been focused on the multiplayer community, adding new units to be used online or in offline skirmishes. Operation Torch brings new scripted missions that trace a set of soldiers moving through North Africa.

After that, though, I ask if Relic plans to continue adding to Company of Heroes 3 or if they're ready to move onto a new project. "Well, it's both actually," CEO Justin Dowdeswell tells me. "We would love to continue with Company of Heroes 3 and not solely as a place for us to experiment. That's one of the advantages of being smaller, and being able to make decisions. We're not going to leave Company of Heroes 3. It's an and function. We are going to embark on the next thing."

So, it doesn't sound like Relic are taking anything off their plate…

#3939. "30fps makes sense" for GTA 6, tech analyst says, and anything above that is "asking for trouble"

Rockstar's settled on its frame rate target for a reason

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Rockstar presented GTA 6 at 30fps in every trailer going back years, so it's little surprise that the game will run at that frame rate. But there was some hope that an upgraded console like the PS5 Pro could push things up to at least 40fps, yet Rockstar has apparently confirmed that the PS5 Pro has the same 30fps cap as every other platform. Tech analysts suggest that any frame rate above 30 is likely not feasible for a game as ambitious as Rockstar's latest.

"You've got to consider the frame time budgets," according to Richard Leadbetter of Digital Foundry in a recent podcast discussion. While we, as players, tend to think of frame rates purely in terms of frames per second, game developers have to consider how long it takes to create each individual frame.

"At 30fps they've got 33.3 milliseconds to process the game world, the simulation, all of that stuff," Leadbetter explains. "That's a fair amount of time, but clearly they've decided from a design perspective that they need it. Now, 60fps, you've got to halve that. You've got to do the same job in half the amount of time. It's not viable."

PS5 Pro has substantially more GPU power than the base model, allowing it to offer visual enhancements like better resolutions and frame rates across many games. But the massive open world and richly reactive sandbox of a game like GTA 6 is largely handled by the CPU, an area where the PS5 Pro has only a modest advantage over its amateur counterpart.

"The obvious thing is to accept that and say, 'Well, what about 40fps? It's only 10fps more than 30,'" Leadbetter continues. "But that's not the way it works. 40fps in terms of frame time is 25 milliseconds. It's a halfway point between 33 and 16 or 17. That's still a huge amount of optimization or cutbacks specifically that would be required in order to hit a 25 millisecond frame time."

Why do we care about 40fps at all? Well, most console games target either 30 or 60fps because most modern TVs update the image 60 times per second. If you get exactly one frame every time the screen refreshes – or one frame every two updates – it's a nice, smooth experience. Anything outside of that range will have a subtle but unpleasant judder.

However, many of the best gaming TVs refresh 120 times per second – a refresh rate that opens up a smooth 40fps experience as a possibility. 40fps modes offer a notable leap in responsiveness over 30fps games, without as many visual compromises as you'd typically see in a full 60fps performance mode. It's become my preferred way to play in any big, cinematic game that offers the option.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

GTA 6 would be a perfect fit for a 40fps option, but Rockstar's vision is apparently too ambitious to allow for it. "It's just asking for trouble, really," Leadbetter concludes, "in a game that is already so rich and dense, but also a game where literally anything can happen because of the systemic nature of the experience. So 30fps makes sense."

I want an uglier GTA 6 that runs at 60 FPS – 30 FPS on PS5 and Xbox Series X is more reason to wait for PC

#3938. Nvidia shareholders have filed a lawsuit against the tech company over claims that they were misled regarding CEO Jensen Huang's affair

If I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oh who am I kidding, it is funny! And despite knowing that this won't likely push Nvidia away from AI, I am a bit tickled to hear that the tech company and Huang are on the receiving end of a lawsuit.

The suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm. Kistenmacher is an Nvidia shareholder, and with this suit he's seeking to "recover compensable damages," for himself and other shareholders due to the "precipitous decline in the market value of the Company’s securities." What a palaver! I do not imagine this will be resolved particularly quickly.

As it currently stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere. Nvidia had this to say on the matter: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate."

The concern comes from the person Huang had an affair with, one Alice Huang (no, they aren't related), a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company who have allegedly given Chinese companies Nvidia chips they bought billions of US dollars of. A messy situation to be sure, and one I unconfidently hope brings about the end of AI, somehow.

#3937. Feature: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X

The fun stuff that cropped up along the way, avoiding major story spoilers

By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.

Review GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

This is going to dominate your life for months!

I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the new Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October. While completing the campaign, I inevitibly came across loads of features that surprised me along the way, so I thought I'd use this opportunity to just highlight a few of them.

Some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-new information. In any case, here are the specific features (avoiding story spoilers) that surprised me as I was completing GTA 6 on Xbox Series X:

On this page: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X

Yeah, there's finally a fuel requirement in a GTA game! It's not too invasive, so don't worry, but if you happen to drive a car around the map for an extensive amount of time, you'll be forced to find a gas station and refuel it (a very short cutscene and a press of the RT button). You can also repair your car at gas stations as well, which certainly comes in handy if you've been smashing it around at high speeds!

You can still break into vehicles the old fashioned way - either stealing it mid-drive or smashing a window to gain access - but you can also use a slim-jim to break the lock, or eventually a key cloner to bypass the security entirely. Be aware of vehicles with trackers though, as if you end up going too slow, the tracker will alert the cops to your location.

It's not always enough to escape the cops and stay hidden from them for an extended period of time. If you really want to ensure you'll lose their attention, you'll want to either ditch the car or take it to a "Pay 'n' Spray" outlet, as well as change your outfit. It's possible to partially do this by throwing on some sunglasses and a hat, but the clever move is to stash one or more outfits in your car's trunk that you can switch between at a moment's notice.

While it's impossible to avoid situations in GTA 6 where you'll be engaging in all sorts of criminal activity, you can handle them in various ways. For example, a mission that requires you to take out a bunch of people can be completed by one-shotting them all, but this will raise your criminal profile. Alternatively, leaving your enemies injured but still alive will push you more towards a "Professional" profile. I haven't properly been able to compare how this affects the game yet (I really need to experiment with both sides of the extreme rather than hovering towards the middle), but Rockstar says it alters how the story, world and Jason / Lucia react to you.

I always love when games get creative with music - South of Midnight was one that really impressed me - and GTA 6 is now one of the best examples I can think of. Basically, you get highly-curated pumping tunes playing in the background during things like shootouts and getaways, while more menacing situations can feature a different vibe of soundtrack, sometimes even with lyrics. You might not quite understand the appeal until you play it, but it's actually one of my favourite new features. The use of music in certain cutscenes is awesome as well.

I don't know if I can verify this yet for sure, but the radio stations either appear to change their music selection based on where you are on the map, or based on how far you've progressed into the story. As I spent more time in Vice City, I started to notice a much bigger range of songs on the Flash FM channel (my favourite) including everyone from Coldplay to The Ting Tings, whereas those tunes never popped up at the start. Try it for yourself and let me know if I'm right about this!

Any GTA game worth its salt has to come with a whole bunch of minigames, and my favourite so far is the addition of minigolf. I believe there are three 18-hole courses dotted around the map in total, and they're beautifully detailed and themed, with genuinely enjoyable holes to play on. There's actual golf as well, but I have to admit I haven't had chance to check it out yet. Pool in the bars is great fun too!

If you really take your time to play through GTA 6, which I highly recommend you do, you'll truly be able to appreciate just how much effort has gone into some of the seemingly smallest aspects of it. Snapmatic, which is the social media platform on your in-game phone, is constantly being updated with new statuses, photos, videos, comments and more, and you could literally just sit just browsing it for ages and enjoying the interactions. There's also a "News" app that regularly gets updated with fresh articles about what's going on in Leonida.

When you get to a certain mission in GTA 6, you'll be introduced to your first video game inside the game itself, which seems to be a very high-brow parody of modern-day indie hits. There are actually multiple games you can play, including one that's very reminiscent of Xbox title Yet Another Zombie Survivors, and these can either be accessed by turning on your TV or going up to arcade cabinets located in various stores all over the map.

When GTA 5 came out for Xbox 360 back in 2013, one of the big things I can recall is how slow the initial loading screens would be, especially once GTA Online got involved. We obviously haven't got an online component to GTA 6 just yet, but in terms of loading up the single-player game on Xbox Series X, it's actually a very quick process that isn't painful whatsoever. You barely even notice it!

Of course, these aren't the only surprising features you'll run into while playing GTA 6 - there are literally hundreds and hundreds that are waiting to be discovered. I don't want to spoil anything about the story or the details of the missions themselves though, and ultimately this is a game where surprises will continue being revealed long into the future.

For now, just go and enjoy it on your Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S (or PS5), and I urge you to take your time and really let it all soak in. One of the perils of reviewing games is that you have to grind to the finish line, and while that does still give you a great impression of the experience, I already can't wait to go back and spend 100+ hours with it this time.

Review GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

#3936. Marathon is becoming a whole new game next month with a roguelite PvE mode, a beta for a very Halo-esque team deathmatch mode, a vibey social space and more

Marathon is getting a lot bigger next month. In September, Bungie outlined their plans for the shooter making some big promises, namely the arrival of a PvE mode, and now they've shown off what you can expect from its next season, Symbiosis.

Top of the order is that PvE mode, which has a name now: Expedition. It's a roguelite mode, one that's playable in co-op, though a lack of details at this current time doesn't make it clear as to whether you can run it solo or not. The season's trailer, which you can have a gander at below, gives off the impression that you'll have to complete particular tasks before exfiltrating like you normally do. I'm sure we'll learn more in time.

The previously promised social space will be coming with this update too, and it's called Limbo. Morbidly appropriate! You can hang out here with your buds, head to a mini arena for some impromptu matches (I think), or head to the firing range where you can test out your weapons. You'll also be able to try out the new runner shell, Bishop, a cooler than you, samurai-sword-wielding robot who can jump real good and do that cool movie thing where it slices a whole bunch of enemies at once in one swing real quick like.

What will undoubtedly have some folks going "Halo's back!" is the beginning of a beta test for a team deathmatch mode. The Halo comparison is apt not simply because of the fact that it's Bungie who are making it, but because there's a deep-voiced announcer guy talking about all the sick kills you do. Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few new weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, big ole alien enemies to take on.

You've still got a little while to wait for Symbiosis, which is currently slated to launch on December 8th. The game will be free to play from then until December 15th, too, obviously in a bid to show sceptics how good it is now (hopefully it is good, for Bungie's sake).

#3935. Review: GTA 6 (PS5) - The Greatest Open World Game Ever Made

What does eight years and an estimated $1 billion get you? Well, GTA 6.

In this long-anticipated crime sandbox, Rockstar has assembled the most technologically accomplished open world ever made, expanding on its groundbreaking work with Red Dead Redemption 2.

But crucially, with its dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, it’s grown up a bit.

This is the franchise at its most mature, shedding the cartoonish cultural caricatures of GTA 5 without losing the biting social commentary the series is known for.

The fictional state of Leonida is undoubtedly the star here; a dense and gigantic urban sandbox populated by an unfathomable array of art assets.

Whether it’s the easy-living coastal island of Key Lento or the mean streets of Crosstown, Rockstar’s artistry is utterly unprecedented.

Zoom in and you’ll see insects attracted to discarded food wrappers; a single convenience store has more unique art assets than entire districts in other open world games. This is remarkable stuff, delivered at such a scale it’s going to leave other publishers with their heads in their hands.

It feels alive, too; a casual visit to a gas station saw me berated by a cyclist for my wayward driving (I told him to chill out), while a brief pause on the side-walk ended up with my car getting hijacked by a masked criminal.

In over 150 hours of play, I’m still discovering random events that add depth and character to the open world. And even when the scripting is pushed to the background, the way every NPC feels designed, with distinctive personality and unique body types, makes this package an unfathomable feat.

But while Leonida is the standout, Jason and Lucia are the vehicles that guide you through it.

Just like GTA 5, each character has their own individual life, but the game is at its best when it brings them together.

I’ve never seen romance made into a mechanic quite like this, aside from perhaps the handholding in ICO, which is repurposed here. (Complete with DualSense haptic feedback when the characters touch.)

Jason is a bit of a beige blank slate, but Lucia brings genuine “girl power” to the story without pandering or feeling insincere.

In fact, in contrast to past GTAs, the many women in this instalment feel much more believable; the game frequently flips expectations on their head, without it ever coming across as forced.

A secret twist revealed in the opening moments adds gravity to the couple’s situation and becomes the driving force behind the story, which takes the pair from pillar to post, fulfilling the whims of a ragtag roster of ne’er-do-wells.

The campaign does fall into cliche territory at times, as the pair bounce from one bad idea to another in order to fulfil their ultimate ambition, and it’s something the characters seem to acknowledge. (“When are we going to get to call our own shots?” Jason wearily ponders at one point.)

But the mission design remains inventive throughout, regularly adding bespoke mechanics and interactions to keep things fresh.

In one early mission, Jason indulges his inner-PowerWash Simulator, as he rinses down a boat while other characters commentate key plot points. I won’t spoil the best moments, but needless to say there are missions here that will be remembered for a long time.

There’s also a slate of optional pastimes running concurrently to the main campaign which add genuine variety to the sandbox.

I was most enamoured by Jason’s home entertainment setup, which includes a distinctly PS4 coded console that can be powered up. I’ll leave you to discover his selection of fully playable games.

But beyond that, the ability to go hunting or even play a round of golf means you can lose yourself in this sandbox for hours at a time, and never really tire of the activities available to you.

Some of the action sequences remind me of all-time classics like Uncharted 3 – fist-pumping, set-piece heavy rollercoaster rides that push Rockstar’s engine to its limits, all within the confines of a meticulously designed open world.

Controller response is vastly superior to the studio’s previous games, with the cover shooting system feeling much more natural and the aiming mechanics buoyed by a pretty fun “bullet time” mechanic.

However, the game does fall into the trap of introducing heavily armoured bullet sponge enemies towards its conclusion, as it runs out of ways to make human-on-human encounters interesting.

That said, I really appreciated the agency GTA 6 gives you over how you approach each situation; non-vitals can be targeted to incapacitate enemies without murdering them, while it’s perfectly possible to sneak in and out of many areas without ever being detected.

This all builds a criminal profile which changes how the police and wider world will interact with you. Meanwhile, you can influence Jason and Lucia’s relationship itself, opting to keep them close or distant depending on how you want things to play out.

An early optional objective allows you to decorate Jason’s idyllic beach house in anticipation of Lucia’s arrival. Complete it in time and the couple will grow closer; ignore it and she’ll acknowledge you didn’t go the extra mile.

Other interactions are subtler: a kiss and cuddle on the balcony of the pair’s Vice City penthouse will strengthen their bond, but it’s up to you whether you want to invest in their relationship or not.

Multiple endings mean there are actual consequences to your actions, even if some decisions along the way feel more like an illusion than something truly meaningful.

The plot does begin to drag in its latter phases, and I do think Rockstar could have tightened up the roughly 60 hour storyline, which will likely take the average player around 80 hours to complete when accounting for the vast amount of side content as well.

(A 100% save could take anywhere up to 300 hours or more, depending on how much support you get from guides.)

As a crime sandbox, I also wanted to mention the ‘Wanted’ system, which has come on leaps and bounds.

A coordinated robbery can be accomplished without ever triggering a traditional car chase, as the game accounts for your outfit, vehicle, weapons, and much more.

Successfully scouting out your targets, and planning accordingly with a change of clothes and getaway car, can see you slip past the police undetected. Few moments in gaming are more satisfying than when you casually drive past a fleet of incoming cop cars, with a bag of successfully looted narcotics in your trunk.

Some players may respond negatively to the life sim elements here, which reward you for exercising and require you to occasionally put gas in your car or eat something.

But I think it adds to the immersive nature of the open world, and concessions have been made to the realism when it makes sense; a quick request to Scooter Bros, for example, will see your favourite car instantaneously delivered to your current location, so you don’t have to wait around.

The biggest downside to the outright awesome spectacle of the open world is that it runs at 30fps on the PS5 Pro, with no option to double the frame rate or tailor the presentation to taste, as has become standard in most other games.

Objectively this is disappointing, but given the sheer scale of Leonida I think it’s a necessary compromise.

It should be noted that despite all this, the frame pacing is solid and the game feels smooth and responsive as a result. I encountered very few (if any) instances of slowdown – even when flying over the map in a jet or speeding down highways being chased by rival gangs.

The audio presentation matches the high standards of the visuals, with different engine growls depending on how you’ve modified your vehicle. (Midnight Club fans may be excited to learn the racing missions here rival most dedicated franchises like Need for Speed alone.)

There are multiple fist-pumping audio cues, which leverage the title’s enormous licensed soundtrack to excellent effect. But credit must also go to composer duo Justice, who bring their distinct brand of disco-inspired electronica to the soundscape, elevating some of the best missions to impressive highs.

And I was blown away by how much texture the DualSense adds, with one of my favourite features being the feedback you feel when you pass cars at speed on the highway. The only thing I didn’t like was the use of adaptive triggers, which feel far too stiff and lack the nuance of first-party games.

GTA 6 is the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2.

Rockstar has set a new sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time.

Crucially, despite the 30fps cap, the gameplay feels responsive and you have much more authorship over how you want to approach it. I enjoyed preparing for my robberies and feeling like I was rewarded for the legwork.

The audiovisual presentation is a new high for the industry, with a frankly flabbergasting array of art assets bringing it all to life.

But I think Jason and Lucia’s ragtag romance, which is central to everything in the game, also demonstrates an unexpected maturity – without completely removing the silly sense of downright dumb humour the series is known for.

Despite unprecedented expectations, GTA 6 delivers – and then some.

#3934. Firaxis lays off 30% of staff with the next XCOM game reportedly struggling

It's been six years since the last full-on XCOM installment, and as it turns out, another is in the works. However, I wouldn't get too excited, because, sadly, developer Firaxis Games is reportedly undergoing hefty layoffs, leaving the future of the sci-fi strategy project a tad uncertain.

Jason Schreier of Bloomberg is reporting that some 30% of the Firaxis workforce was laid off as of today, November 17. That amounts to somewhere in the region of 60 staff, and owner Take-Two confirmed that Heather Hazen is vacating the role of studio head.

People familiar with the matter say a new XCOM is part of the company's current slate, but there have been problems with the game's development of late. These purportedly include failing to hit a major milestone over the summer.

Apparently, development of the as-yet-unnamed XCOM will continue, but there may be changes as a result of the rejig. Losing that many devs, it's hard to imagine any games in the works at Firaxis being shielded from some sort of reverberations, however minor or ultimately inconsequential.

"Firaxis is restructuring and re-centering around the studio’s core strength - designing world-class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years," a statement from Take-Two reads. "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis."

These layoffs are occurring on the eve of GTA 6's release, a tectonic shift across the entire entertainment world. Rockstar, another subsidiary of Take-Two, has been printing money for the last decade-plus thanks to GTA 5 and GTA Online, and is now about to do even more so.

How and when this new XCOM is announced remains to be seen. Likewise, questions linger about the ongoing support for Civilization 7 and other entries in the series. Watch this space for further updates.

#3933. Ahead of GTA 6 and as concerns over genAI PC ports grow, Take-Two's CEO says they're revving up their "technical defences" and "legal activites" over piracy

"[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that"

It's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain company finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are currently technically and legally preparing themselves.

IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business issues they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended."

Zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he said.

It was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it."

Essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

#3932. Missing teenager rescued after reaching out to another player in Among Us

"Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim."

A teenager who went missing in Utah more than 17 months ago has been rescued from a home in Oregon after she got in touch with another young player in Among Us.

According to a federal criminal complaint reported by Newsweek and KUTV (via IGN), the girl, who was 15 when she disappeared from Garden City, Utah, on 29th May 2025, began chatting with another teenager in Among Us on or around 15th October this year.

The pair later moved their conversation to a different social media app, where she told them who she was and that she was being held against her will in Oregon. She had been given a phone with no cellular data, which meant she could only get online via wi-fi.

The other teen told their parent, who contacted the FBI on 1st November. Agents listened in on a video call between the parent and the girl, and she was recovered from the house later that day. She is now 17.

Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, of Huntington, Oregon, was arrested during a traffic stop.

According to the US Attorney's Office for the District of Utah, he allegedly met the girl online in May 2025, then drove to Utah to pick her up and took her back to his home across state lines. He was charged on 2nd November with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity, and made his first court appearance in Boise, Idaho, on 4th November.

"Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim," said US Attorney Melissa Holyoak. "Those who allegedly exploit and prey upon the most vulnerable members of our communities will be relentlessly investigated and held accountable."

Utah's US Attorney's Office stresses that a complaint is merely an allegation, and that all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

#3931. Sony have cancelled Fairgame$, once again reminding us that chasing live service big bucks basically never works

You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

This comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony said that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

Bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

Sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

For those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was announced back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a new name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

#3930. GTA 6 Comparison Shows Difference Between Xbox Series X And Series S

Here's how Grand Theft Auto 6 looks across both Xbox consoles

Update [Wed 18th Nov 2026, 3:19pm]: Digital Foundry has also shared an analysis of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X|S today, and you can watch their video at the top of this article. We've covered it in more depth elsewhere on Pure Xbox too:

News Three Big Takeaways From Digital Foundry's GTA 6 Analysis For Xbox Series X|S

Original Story: With GTA 6 reviews now out in the wild, and countless Xbox players already getting access to it via the controversial New Zealand trick, it's no surprise that we've also got loads of screenshots and clips doing the rounds online.

One of the best sources for raw Xbox gameplay footage is the YouTube channel Fuzion Xbox Testing, and they're already uploaded their initial look at both the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S versions of GTA 6.

On Xbox Series X, it's very much what you'd expect - a really amazing-looking game with an internal resolution of 1440p, upscaled to 4K. The 30FPS performance is largely smooth, but does drop frames on occasion.

I also played GTA 6 on Xbox Series X for our Pure Xbox review, and here's what I said about it:

"Of course, it's almost a given at this point that GTA 6 looks visually incredible, and I can confirm that it's definitely a stunner on Xbox Series X. There's some occasional pop-in, but it's minimal, and I only ran into a few tiny bugs during the review period (which may have been ironed out for release anyway). The performance is mostly very smooth considering the circumstances as well..."

"It should be noted that I played around 30 hours on a VRR-enabled display during the review period, and around 10 hours without one. I was perfectly happy with the performance in both cases, with the only noticeably big frame rate drops occurring during very rare and visually intensive gameplay sequences."

On Xbox Series S, GTA 6 still looks really impressive from a visual standpoint, even though some drawbacks have clearly been made in terms of ray tracing and texture quality. The frame rate in the game's initial opening is shown to be a locked 30FPS in some sequences, dropping into the mid-20s during busier moments.

Overall though, the feedback we've seen from Xbox Series S players thus far has been very positive, especially in terms of how impressive the game looks. Rockstar Games actually talked to Wccftech about the Series S version as well, revealing they're using AMD FSR Upscaling 4 to scale the resolution to 1080p.

"On the Xbox Series S, we’re starting from a base resolution of 720p, which is scaled to 1080p using AMD FSR Upscaling 4."

"...[our] focus on lighting made it vital for us to ensure we could use the same lighting solution on each console, including the Xbox Series S, where memory pressure posed a bit of a challenge. The results made that a challenge worth overcoming."

Great stuff, then! We'll leave you with the comparison footage for GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S down below.

#3929. Saving Mass Effect would take $200m+, says BioWare co-founder

Anyone hoping to buy Mass Effect from EA and finish what BioWare started needs to get saving now, as it could cost over $200 million (£150m).

That's according to BioWare co-founder Trent Oster, who reckons that's what a new Mass Effect game would need to meet fans' expectations.

"The scary component of Mass Effect is the audience is going to want the best of 'AAA' development," Oster said on Twitter/X, as spotted by GamesRadar.

The scary component of Mass Effect is the audience is going to want the best of “AAA” development. Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200M+. That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work.

"Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200M+. That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work."

He did add that it could be done for less, though. "That said, I think it can be done well for less than that amount with a disciplined approach and an experienced team," Oster said.

"I think a game could be done cheaper, if you kept it simple and hit the big beats," he added in a separate tweet. "It wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept. The big push would be getting the IP free. The fans deserve more than one game."

I think a game could be done cheaper, if you kept it simple and hit the big beats. It wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept. The big push would be getting the IP free. The fans deserve more than one game.

Oster's comments come as the #SaveMassEffect campaign continues to grow following EA's decision to close BioWare and cancel Mass Effect 5. Fans want EA to keep making Mass Effect games, or hand the series over to a studio that will.

Oster has backed the campaign too. "I love seeing all the energy around #SaveMassEffect," he wrote on 4th November. "I think there is a still a great thesis for a well-funded RPG developer who can deliver. Makes me want to get some of the original band back together."

EA has not confirmed whether or not it would consider selling the IP.

The petition created to save BioWare's well-loved sci-fi RPG, Mass Effect, topped 185,000 signatures in just days. It's now exceeded 317,000. Joe Smith, credited with starting the petition, isn't necessarily asking EA to change its mind about BioWare; instead, the petition calls for "decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect".

We said a sad farewell to BioWare last month. The closure, which came just months after Saudi Arabia's $55bn leveraged buyout of EA, was anticipated by experts, but drew widespread condemnation and messages of sympathy from across the industry.

A new report claims EA closed BioWare because it was forced to choose between investing in one of two sci-fi projects: a new Mass Effect game or a new Star Wars Battlefront game. And it chose the latter.

Fans are trying other routes to keep BioWare's doors open, too. Canadian fans of the studio have escalated their grievances to the governmental level, calling on the Canadian Government to step in and save the studio from closure, seemingly after Canada's New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis called on the government to do so.

Right, today's been miserable thanks to the now hourly discourse we have to all take part in lest we be seen as approving of the current bad thing, how about something that looks simply pleasant? I've been enamoured by the vibe of Tanuki: Pon's Summer since it was announced in no small part because of how in some small ways it reminds me of Boku No Natsuyasumi, a cult-classic, Japan-only game series that's mostly just about hanging out in the Japanese countryside. This one isn't so lackadaisical, as you do have a job to do in delivering mail, but I think a similar spirit is there.

When it comes to delivering mail, there is a Death Strandingian element to it in your need to place your boxes on your BMX (which you can do sick tricks and flips on, of course) to maximise how much you can deliver. A bit less stressful than Kojima's joint, obviously, though elements are still there. Any money you earn from this gig can then be spent on restoring the shrine that you oh so love, which falls onto the sim side of things with the ability to fully customise how the shrine looks.

There are also a whole heap of minigames to perform that helps you get to know the locals. I'm talking baseball, sumo wrestling, working in a sushi restaurant and, of course, fishing. You can see bits of that in the launch trailer above, which comes with as 2010s an anime opening song you could wish for with some animation so good it makes me want an adaptation of the game.
